nina: quick sync 60 for onboarding. The enterprise buyer wants explicit answers for: key escrow, key rotation automation, support for external HSMs, and timeline for rewrapping cached model state during cutover.

chris: Key escrow: we don't escrow customer KEKs. Customers keep control of KEKs. For Hosted CMEK, keys live in customer's cloud KMS account. For Private, they live in your HSM.

lee: Rotation automation options: 1) recommended pattern is canary rewrap + staged roll; 2) we can run rewrap job as part of a maintenance window; 3) if customer wants, we can provide a Rewrap-as-a-Service engagement.

security-cust: Our audit requires proof that Redwood doesn't export key material. Any standard language we can include?

chris: Contract bullet: "Provider will not request, store, or export customer key encryption key (KEK) raw material. Provider will only perform cryptographic operations (GenerateDataKey, Encrypt/Decrypt) against KEKs in the customer's KMS or HSM, acting under principals authorized by the customer."

nina: For the cutover timeline 10: we should size rewrap work by amount of persisted data. For caches it can be minutes to hours; for large archives might be longer. Suggest we say: typical rewrap of active working set during cutover: 30\r-2h (depending on size); full archive rewrap: schedule-dependent.
